summary: KV-cache lock contention causing SSE/WebSocket chat stream to stall mid-generation
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using the dedicated cluster for Syntaxly report streaming chat (SSE and WebSocket) sessions stalling mid-generation. The generation process continues on the worker (model tokens advance) but clients stop receiving chunks for ~10-30s, then either receive a burst of tokens or the connection is closed. Impact affects a subset of long-context sessions that exercise prefix/KV cache heavily.

Impact:
- Multiple customers using dedicated clusters experienced degraded user-facing streaming with partial token delivery and timeouts for long responses.
- Symptoms occur intermittently under sustained bursty traffic and while background cache eviction/compaction is active.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool in prod | us-east-1
- Customer: Syntaxly (dedicated tenant)
- Models observed: redwood/vicuna-13b (main), redwood/vicuna-7b (also observed)

Observed behavior:
- Client SSE/WebSocket receives initial tokens, then stream silence for 10-30s while server logs show continuing generation activity; afterwards either a token burst or stream closure with 499/502 seen at proxies.
- Internal worker metrics show increased mutex wait times on kv-cache locks concurrent with GC/eviction cycles.

Expected behavior:
- Continuous streaming with small inter-chunk intervals (<200ms typical) and graceful fallback if worker evicted.

Steps to reproduce (high-level):
1) On a dedicated customer pool, start a long chat generation with ~8k prompt + multi-turn history that hits prefix cache reads.
2) Send multiple near-simultaneous streaming requests from different clients to increase contention on cache read/write paths.
3) Observe one or more streams stalling mid-generation while worker logs progress.
steps_to_reproduce: Provision a dedicated cluster in us-east-1 (or use Syntaxly replica).
Load a long-context conversation (~8k tokens) and ensure prefix cache entries are created.
From 3+ clients send streaming requests simultaneously that reuse prefixes (e.g., same system prompts with per-turn deltas).
Monitor SSE/WebSocket client for mid-generation silence and check worker logs for kv_cache lock wait messages.
logs: [2026-03-12T15:21:03Z] serving-runtime[worker-7]: generation: step=312 emit_chunk size=128 status=blocked kv_cache: lock_wait=312ms
[2026-03-12T15:21:33Z] nginx[proxy-12]: upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.9.2.7, server: redwood-host
[2026-03-12T15:21:34Z] serving-runtime[worker-7]: generation: token=... continued after lock (burst emit 220 tokens)
investigation_notes: 15:30 - Support triaged and confirmed identical symptom with Syntaxly reproducer. Customer provided a request_id and SSE capture.
16:05 - SRE attached flamegraphs from the affected node: top contributor is kv-cache mutex wait during eviction sweep.
16:45 - We observed correlation between eviction/compaction and increased per-request latency in chunk emission; not all nodes show the spike (appears on nodes with heavy shared-prefix reuse).
17:15 - Reproduced locally with stress test that simulates prefix reuse and concurrent updates: measured lock contention and per-chunk emission stalls on the read path when eviction kicks in.
18:00 - Linked to recent kv-cache compaction change (PR 398) that introduced a coalesced eviction pass holding a global lock for longer periods under load.
hypothesis: KV cache compaction/eviction holds a global lock that blocks read path for streams. During compaction, worker threads are blocked waiting on the lock which delays writing stream chunks to the connection; network proxies treat the silence as stalled and sometimes close the connection or a burst of buffered data is delivered later.
customer_impact: Partial stream losses and timeouts for heavy long-context streaming sessions. Reported by Syntaxly (enterprise) customers in production; estimated 3-7% of streaming requests in peak windows for that tenant.
workaround: Short-term: reduce cache compaction frequency and/or increase kv-cache shard count for affected dedicated pool. For customer Syntaxly, we temporarily disabled compaction on their pool which reduced occurrences. Also recommended client-side reconnect-with-offset fallback in their SDK until fix is rolled out.
estimated_next_steps: Back out or patch PR 398 that increased compaction lock duration and ship a lock-free read path for compaction (engineering).
Prepare a hotfix PR to reduce compaction batch size and add metrics for lock hold time (priority).
Schedule rolling restart of affected serving nodes after patch to avoid transient lock states (SRE).
Communicate mitigation and ETA to customer success and Syntaxly.
resolution_notes: (in progress) Hotfix branch created for kv-cache with fine-grained compaction locks. Initial tests show removal of >200ms lock waits under stress. Rolling patch targeted for 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC with low-traffic window. Will update after deployment and customer validation.
